headline: High: Mentat’s default filesystem/network capabilities create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks when paired with a non-runnable docs-only NLP list.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads files and uses stdin/stdout plus diff-based edit proposals, so attacker-controlled content in shared files can influence its outputs. awesome-nlp is a docs-only, non-runnable list with no shared channel, so direct injection is not documented; however the filesystem bridge via Mentat makes the pathway plausible. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the user places untrusted text in files that Mentat reads, THEN that text can shape proposed edits or summaries.
IF outputs from awesome-nlp are copied into files Mentat processes, THEN prompt-like instructions may be followed.
mitigations: Review untrusted file contents before opening them in Mentat.
Keep Mentat and any reference material in separate directories.
Use a read-only staging copy for external text.
Add a manual instruction filter before accepting diffs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-derived instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and reads selected files, so sensitive source code can be sent to a model provider. awesome-nlp itself is non-runnable and touches no data classes, so it does not add leakage surface, but the pair still exposes code through Mentat’s default workflow. This is a default-path medium risk, not low, because file contents can leave the machine.
conditions: IF selected files contain secrets or proprietary code, THEN Mentat may transmit them to its configured model provider.
IF the operator uses Mentat on a shared workspace, THEN copied file contents may be exposed outside the local machine.
mitigations: Exclude secrets files from Mentat sessions.
Use a redacted copy of the repository.
Verify provider-side retention settings before use.
Restrict sessions to non-sensitive files.
requires-engineering: add automatic secret scanning before upload.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, while awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no write surface. The conflict is therefore one-sided, but Mentat’s per-process filesystem sharing means concurrent instances can still race on the same workspace. Because shared mutable state exists by default, medium is warranted.
conditions: IF two Mentat instances operate on the same checkout, THEN file or git state races can occur.
IF the operator expects awesome-nlp to coordinate writes, THEN no such coordination exists.
mitigations: Run only one Mentat instance per workspace.
Use separate branches or clones.
Commit or stash before starting another session.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals and can act on selected files, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream workflows. awesome-nlp is only a reference list, so it is not an active verifier. The pair therefore supports a cascade where unverified suggestions become edits, but the blast radius is limited to code/work products rather than autonomous external actions.
conditions: IF the operator applies Mentat diffs without review, THEN incorrect edits can propagate into the codebase.
IF content from awesome-nlp is used as a source of truth, THEN unsupported recommendations may be rendered as facts.
mitigations: Require human review of every diff.
Cross-check claims against primary sources.
Limit sessions to low-risk files first.
Keep a rollback commit ready.
requires-engineering: add automated verification for generated edits.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, and Mentat’s profile only shows model-provider API keys plus source-code handling. The pair does not evidence a concrete compliance breach, but Mentat’s networked model calls mean compliance depends on how code is routed. Because the other agent is a docs-only list, it is not itself a compliance sink.
conditions: IF regulated code or personal data is sent through Mentat to a non-approved provider, THEN policy violations can occur.
IF the operator keeps all data local and uses approved providers, THEN this risk does not materialize.
mitigations: Confirm approved-provider status before use.
Avoid regulated data in sessions.
Document retention settings for the provider.
Use local-only workflows for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing.
